description: Teetool models spatial variability in collections of trajectories. Willem Johannis Eerland and collaborators provide Python routines that represent paths with Gaussian processes and derive mean paths and confidence regions from their covariance. The repository links examples and documentation for two- and three-dimensional trajectories. Geographic extent and spatial resolution follow the input paths, but the own README explicitly says temporal effects are ignored. The model can support related transport or flight-corridor simulations by characterizing spatial dispersion and overlap. Code is free under MIT, with numerical, plotting and three-dimensional visualization dependencies listed. A limitation is that spatial overlap does not by itself imply simultaneous occupancy or a time-resolved collision probability. The README also marks some operating-system setup instructions as unchecked for the latest version. No path observations or example data were downloaded and no confidence region was calculated.
